gaps.sentence: She ___ her grandmother every Sunday; it is a promise she never breaks.
gaps.hint: every Sunday marks repeated routine action
gaps.explanation: 'Every Sunday' signals a regularly repeated action, so the present simple is correct: visits.

gaps.sentence: She ___ to the gym three times a week, mostly before work.
gaps.hint: three times a week shows a routine
gaps.explanation: Frequency expressions like 'three times a week' describe habits, which take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: At the moment, the council ___ whether to sell the library.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows an ongoing process
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' marks an ongoing process, so the present continuous fits: is deciding.

gaps.sentence: The conference ___ on Monday and ends on Wednesday.
gaps.explanation: Fixed schedules are stated in the present simple: starts.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: I usually walk to work, but today I ___ the bus because it is raining.
gaps.hint: today contrasts with the usual habit
gaps.explanation: 'But today' signals a temporary break from habit, so the present continuous is correct: am taking.

gaps.sentence: When we were students, we ___ to live on instant noodles.
gaps.hint: a past habit with used to
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' plus the infinitive describes a past habit: used to live.

gaps.sentence: By the time I woke up, my flatmates ___ to work.
gaps.hint: by the time plus past simple
gaps.explanation: 'By the time' plus a past action refers back to an earlier past action, so the past perfect is needed: had gone.
